info.name: FilmLog API
info.description:
REST API documentation for the FilmLog movie watchlist (TypeScript + Express + Prisma 7 + PostgreSQL).

RUN ORDER
Run the folders top-to-bottom, or use the Collection Runner. Each folder depends on variables captured by the previous one:
  01 Auth        -> saves {{token}}
  02 Movies      -> saves {{movieId}}
  04 Watched     -> saves {{reviewId}}, {{tokenB}}

REQUIREMENTS
- Server running: `npm run dev` (default http://localhost:8000)
- Database seeded: `npm run db:seed` (20 movies, ids 1..20)
- Environment "FilmLog Local" selected

NOTE ON SIDE EFFECTS
A full run registers two throwaway users (`postman_a_<timestamp>@test.local` and `postman_b_<timestamp>@test.local`). There is no user-delete endpoint, so those rows remain in the database.

item.name: 01 · Auth
item.description:
Registration and login.

`Register A` generates a unique timestamped email in a pre-request script, so the folder can be re-run without hitting 409.

`Login A` stores the JWT in the environment variable `{{token}}`, which every protected folder then uses.

exec: // Unique per run so re-running never collides with an existing account.
pm.test('never echoes the password hash', function () {

request.description:
Creates a user.

**Expect:** `201 Created`

```json
{
  "id": "885263f1-1126-4272-9969-1b79b220c4bf",
  "email": "postman_a_1794110580@test.local",
  "username": "postman-user-a",
  "createdAt": "2026-11-08T04:03:00.883Z"
}
```

Validation (`src/middlewares/validate.middleware.ts`):
- `email` — must contain `@` and a dot in the domain, max 254 chars
- `password` — 6-128 chars, **not** trimmed
- `username` — 1-50 chars, trimmed

**Errors:** `400` validation, `409` email already registered.

No token is returned — registering does not log you in; call `Login A` next.

exec: pm.test('returns a JWT and the public user', function () {
pm.test('the user object has no password hash', function () {
// Every protected folder depends on this variable.

request.description:
Exchanges credentials for a JWT.

**Expect:** `200 OK`

```json
{
  "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...",
  "user": {
    "id": "885263f1-1126-4272-9969-1b79b220c4bf",
    "email": "postman_a_1794110580@test.local",
    "username": "postman-user-a",
    "createdAt": "2026-11-08T04:03:00.883Z"
  }
}
```

The token payload is `{ "sub": "<userId>", "iat": ..., "exp": ... }` — a 7-day expiry by default. The test script stores it as `{{token}}`.

**Errors:** `400` validation, `401 Invalid email or password`.

Unknown email and wrong password return the **same** 401 body on purpose, to avoid account enumeration.

exec: pm.test('returns the caller identity from the token', function () {

request.description:
Returns the authenticated user's profile.

**Expect:** `200 OK`

```json
{
  "id": "885263f1-1126-4272-9969-1b79b220c4bf",
  "email": "postman_a_1794110580@test.local",
  "username": "postman-user-a",
  "createdAt": "2026-11-08T04:03:00.883Z"
}
```

Identity comes from the token subject (`sub`), never from the request body.

**Errors:** `401` missing/expired token, `401 Account no longer exists` if the user was deleted after the token was issued.

item.name: 02 · Movies
item.description:
Public catalogue endpoints. No authentication required.

The first request captures `{{movieId}}` for the watchlist and review folders.

exec: pm.test('each row has the full movie shape', function () {

request.description:
Full catalogue, ordered by `id` ascending.

**Expect:** `200 OK` — an array of 20 movies.

```json
[
  {
    "id": 1,
    "title": "Inception",
    "year": 2010,
    "director": "Christopher Nolan",
    "genres": ["Sci-Fi", "Action", "Thriller"],
    "rating": 8.8,

    "poster_url": "https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/w500/oYuLEt3zVCKq57qu2F8dT7NIa6f.jpg",
    "cast": ["Leonardo DiCaprio", "Joseph Gordon-Levitt", "Elliot Page", "Tom Hardy"],
```

The test script saves the first movie's `id` as `{{movieId}}`.

exec: pm.test('every result actually has the genre', function () {

query.description: Exact match against one element of the `genres` text[] column.

request.description:
Filters by a single genre.

**Expect:** `200 OK` — 7 movies for `Sci-Fi` (ids 1, 4, 8, 12, 13, 16, 18).

Uses Prisma's `{ has: value }` on the Postgres `text[]` column, which is an **exact** element match — `sci-fi` lowercase returns an empty array.

Available genres in the seed: Sci-Fi, Action, Thriller, Drama, Comedy, Crime, Adventure, Animation, Fantasy, Music, Horror, Family, Mystery, History, Biography.

query.description: Case-insensitive substring match on title OR director.

request.description:
Case-insensitive substring search across `title` and `director`.

**Expect:** `200 OK` — 5 movies for `nolan`:

```
Inception | The Dark Knight | Interstellar | Memento | Oppenheimer
```

`genre` and `search` combine as AND when both are sent.

Single movie by id.

**Expect:** `200 OK` with the full movie object.

**Errors:**
- `400 ID must be a whole number` — non-numeric id (`/movies/abc`)
- `400 ID must be a positive whole number` — `0` or negative
- `404 Movie not found` — valid integer, no such row (`/movies/999`)

item.name: 03 · Watchlist 🔒
item.description:
Watched-later list. Every request requires `Authorization: Bearer {{token}}`.

Responses are **flat**: `{ ...movie, movieId, createdAt }` — the movie fields sit at the top level.

request.description:
The caller's watchlist, newest first.

**Expect:** `200 OK`

```json
[
  {
    "id": 1,
    "title": "Inception",
    "year": 2010,
    "director": "Christopher Nolan",
    "genres": ["Sci-Fi", "Action", "Thriller"],
    "rating": 8.8,
    "duration": "148 min",
    "synopsis": "Seorang pencuri ulung...",
    "poster_url": "https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/w500/...jpg",
    "cast": ["Leonardo DiCaprio", "..."],
    "createdAt": "2026-11-08T04:03:01.260Z",
    "movieId": 1
  }
]
```

Note `id` is the **movie** id; `movieId` repeats it and `createdAt` is the watchlist entry's timestamp. Scoped to the token's user — you never see another user's rows. Empty array if nothing added.

exec: pm.test('returns the flattened movie entry', function () {

request.description:
Adds a movie to the caller's watchlist.

**Expect:** `201 Created` with the flattened entry.

Body accepts both `movieId` and `movie_id` (alias), because the bundled frontend sends either.

**Errors:**
- `400` — `movieId` missing / not a whole number
- `404 Movie not found` — the movie does not exist
- `409 Movie is already in your watchlist` — enforced by `@@unique([userId, movieId])`

`userId` is **never** read from the body; it comes from the token. Any extra keys are stripped by the validation middleware.

Removes a movie from the watchlist.

**Expect:** `204 No Content` — empty body.

**Errors:**
- `400` — `movieId` is not a positive whole number
- `404 Movie is not in your watchlist` — no such entry for this user

Uses `deleteMany` rather than `delete`, so a missing row returns `count: 0` and becomes an explicit 404 instead of a Prisma `P2025`.

item.name: 04 · Watched 🔒
item.description:
Watch history + reviews. Every request requires a token.

Responses are **nested**: `{ ...review, movie }` — the movie is under `movie`. This is the opposite shape of the watchlist, matching what the bundled frontend reads.

This folder also registers and logs in **User B**, whose token is used for the 403 case in folder 05.

request.description:
The caller's reviews, newest first.

**Expect:** `200 OK`

```json
[
  {
    "id": "bd4eb2f2-15d7-450f-81e2-2979c97d044a",
    "userId": "2d1c7a23-90d9-4d93-a6d0-e88580f486ac",
    "movieId": 2,
    "rating": 5,
    "review": "Bagus sekali",
    "createdAt": "2026-11-08T04:03:06.666Z",
    "movie": {
      "id": 2,
      "title": "Parasite",
      "year": 2019,
      "director": "Bong Joon-ho",
      "genres": ["Drama", "Thriller", "Comedy"],
      "rating": 8.5,
      "duration": "132 min",
      "synopsis": "Keluarga Kim yang miskin...",
      "poster_url": "https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/w500/...jpg",
      "cast": ["Song Kang-ho", "..."],
      "createdAt": "2026-11-07T09:31:56.501Z"
    }
  }
]
```

Shaped as `{ ...review, movie }` because the frontend reads `item.movie` first.

exec: pm.test('returns the review with a nested movie', function () {
// Folder 05 uses this for the 403 and 204 cases.

request.description:
Records a movie as watched, with a 1-5 star rating and a written review.

**Expect:** `201 Created`

```json
{
  "id": "bd4eb2f2-15d7-450f-81e2-2979c97d044a",
  "userId": "2d1c7a23-90d9-4d93-a6d0-e88580f486ac",

  "createdAt": "2026-11-08T04:03:06.666Z",
  "movie": { "id": 2, "title": "Parasite", ... }
}
```

Implemented as an `upsert` on `@@unique([userId, movieId])`, so **reviewing the same movie again updates it and still returns 201** rather than a 409.

Body accepts `movieId`/`movie_id` and `review`/`opinion`.

**Errors:**
- `400 rating must be between 1 and 5`
- `400 review must not be empty` / too long (max 2000 chars)
- `404 Movie not found`

Registers a **second, unrelated** user.

**Expect:** `201 Created`

This exists only to prove ownership isolation: User B must not be able to delete User A's review (folder 05, `403` case).

The email is timestamped in a pre-request script, so re-running the collection does not hit `409`.

request.description:
Logs in as User B and stores `{{tokenB}}`.

**Expect:** `200 OK` with a JWT.

item.name: 05 · Error Cases
item.description:
One request per status code the API is designed to return. This folder is the visible evidence for the error-handling rubric.

Most of these are **expected to fail** — the assertions check for the failure, not for success.

Order matters: the 409 case leaves a watchlist row behind and cleans it up; the 403 case relies on `{{reviewId}}` from folder 04.

exec: pm.test('message names the real problem', function () {

request.description:
**Expect:** `400 Bad Request`

```json
{
  "message": "Password is too short (at least 6 characters)",
  "errors": ["password: is too short (at least 6 characters)"]
}
```

Two representations of the same failure:
- `message` — human-readable, for toasts and form banners
- `errors[]` — machine-readable, `"field: problem"`

The password is not trimmed before the length check, so `"  a  "` is 5 characters and passes.

exec: pm.test('rejects before reaching the database', function () {

request.description:
**Expect:** `400 Bad Request`

```json
{
  "message": "ID must be a whole number",
  "errors": ["id: must be a whole number"]
}
```

The `:id` param is validated by `isInt(1)` **before** any query runs, so a bad id never reaches Postgres.

Compare `/movies/0`, which returns `400 ID must be a positive whole number`.

**Expect:** `400 Bad Request`

```json
{
  "message": "ID must be a valid UUID",
  "errors": ["id: must be a valid UUID"]
}
```

Review ids are UUIDs (`@default(uuid())`), so the route validates the `:id` shape with `isUuid` before querying. Without this, a junk id would surface as an unrelated Prisma error.

exec: pm.test('says what is wrong with the header', function () {

request.description:
No `Authorization` header at all.

**Expect:** `401 Unauthorized`

```json
{ "message": "Missing or malformed Authorization header" }
```

Auth is applied at the **router mount** (`api.use('/watchlist', requireAuth, ...)`), so no route inside the router can be accidentally left unprotected.

A well-formed header with a token that fails verification.

**Expect:** `401 Unauthorized`

```json
{ "message": "Invalid or expired token" }
```

A token that is valid-but-expired returns a distinct message: `401 Token has expired`, so the client knows to re-authenticate rather than re-register.

Valid integer, no such row.

**Expect:** `404 Not Found`

```json
{ "message": "Movie not found" }
```

The catalogue has ids `1..20` only, so `999` is a deliberately valid-but-absent id. Note the difference from `400`: `999` is well-formed, it just does not exist.

item.name: 409 · Setup 1 — clear any leftover entry (204 or 404 both OK)

exec: // Idempotent setup: removes a leftover row so the duplicate-add below is the
// only source of a 409. 204 = removed, 404 = nothing to remove.

request.description:
**Setup request — not an error case.**

Removes the movie from the watchlist if it is already there.

**Expect:** `204 No Content`, or `404` if it was not present.

This makes the folder re-runnable: without it, a leftover row from a previous run would make the *setup* request return `409` instead of the duplicate request below.

**Setup request — not the error case.**

Adds a movie so the next request has something to duplicate.

**Expect:** `201 Created`

The pre-request script deletes any leftover row first, so re-running the folder is safe.

Adds the **same** movie twice.

**Expect:** `409 Conflict`

```json
{ "message": "Movie is already in your watchlist" }
```

The service checks first for a friendly message; if two requests raced past that check, the database's `@@unique([userId, movieId])` would still reject the second with Prisma `P2002`, which the error handler maps to the same `409`. (P2002 on login/register similarly reads `A record with that email already exists`.)

User **B** (authenticated, `{{tokenB}}`) tries to delete a review owned by User **A** (`{{reviewId}}` from folder 04).

**Expect:** `403 Forbidden`

```json
{ "message": "You can only modify your own reviews" }
```

The three outcomes of this one endpoint:

| Situation | Status |
|---|---|
| No / invalid token | `401` |
| Valid token, not the author | `403` |
| Valid token, is the author | `204` |

Implemented as two queries so "missing" and "not yours" stay distinguishable: `deleteMany({ where: { id, userId } })` would collapse both into `count: 0` and silently turn the 403 into a 404.

**Prerequisite:** folders 01 and 04 must have run (`{{tokenB}}` and `{{reviewId}}` set).

The **owner** (User A, `{{token}}`) deletes the same review that B was refused.

**Expect:** `204 No Content` — empty body.

This is the "before/after" of the 403 case above: identical request, different token, different outcome. Also cleans up the review so the collection can be re-run.

**Errors:** `404 Review not found` if the id is already gone; `400` if the id is not a UUID.

item.name: 422 · AI picked a movie outside the catalogue (documentation only)

exec: // This case CANNOT be forced on demand: Gemini reliably answers with a real
// catalogue id. The request stays in the collection to document the status
// code, and the assertion tolerates the normal 200 so a run never fails here.
pm.test('200 normally, 422 only if the model invents an id', function () {
pm.test('422 explains the catalogue mismatch', function () {
// A 200 must still reference a movie that really exists.
pm.test('the returned movie is real', function () {

request.description:
**Documentation only — do not expect a 422 from a normal run.**

Gemini almost always returns a valid catalogue id, so this request usually answers `200`. It exists to document the status code and its meaning.

**When it does happen:** `422 Unprocessable Entity`

```json
{ "message": "The AI recommended a movie outside the catalogue; please retry" }
```

Why `422` and not `400`: the request body was perfectly valid. The failure happened downstream — the server produced a result it could not fulfil. `400` means "your input is wrong"; `422` means "valid input, unprocessable outcome".

The guard lives in `src/services/recommendation.service.ts`:

```ts
const movie = await prisma.movie.findUnique({ where: { id: parsed.movie_id } });
if (!movie) throw new HttpError(422, 'The AI recommended a movie outside the catalogue; please retry');
```

Prompt rules are probabilistic; this database lookup is deterministic. See `02 · Movies → AI recommendation` for the happy path.

response.name: 422 — hallucinated id (sample)

item.name: 06 · AI Recommendation
item.description:
Gemini-backed recommendation. Public endpoint.

The model is constrained to pick exactly one movie from the local catalogue and the returned id is re-verified against the database.

exec: pm.test('the recommended id exists in the catalogue', function () {

request.description:
Asks Gemini for one movie from the local catalogue.

**Expect:** `200 OK`

```json
{
  "movie_id": 14,
  "reasoning": "Memento adalah pilihan yang tepat karena menyajikan cerita misteri yang sangat kuat...",
  "movie": {
    "id": 14,
    "title": "Memento",
    "year": 2000,
    "director": "Christopher Nolan",
    "genres": ["Mystery", "Thriller"],
    "rating": 8.4,
    "duration": "113 min",
    "synopsis": "Seorang pria yang kehilangan ingatan jangka pendek...",
    "poster_url": "https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/w500/...jpg",
    "cast": ["Guy Pearce", "..."],
    "createdAt": "2026-11-07T09:31:56.501Z"
  }
}
```

**How it stays grounded:**
1. The catalogue is read from Postgres (`findMany`, 6 fields), not hardcoded.
2. The prompt numbers rules, including "if nothing matches, pick the closest" — the escape hatch that stops invention.
3. `responseSchema` + `responseMimeType: application/json` force `{ movie_id, reasoning }` only.
4. The output is re-validated (integer id, non-empty reasoning).
5. The id is looked up in the database; a miss becomes `422`.

Every displayed field comes from the database row, so the model only ever contributes *which id* plus prose.

**Errors:** `400` prompt must be 3-1000 chars · `502` upstream Gemini failure / rejected key · `503` rate limited or empty catalogue.

`prompt` is in Indonesian here; `reasoning` comes back in the same language.
